title: wringer.judgement.v2
description: A person's answers to the requirements only a person can judge — v2, the pen failing closed (0.6.1, run 3 F11/F12). WHY v2 EXISTS: run 3 measured `wringer-board judge --verdict met` recording a verdict after the declared `show:` command had FAILED (`/bin/sh: python: command not found`) — the product recorded that a person saw and approved something it failed to display. v1 is published and frozen (law 7: a byte change without a new schema_version is a silent break for every reader), so the display facts arrive as a NEW schema, and every v1 record remains readable by every reader that accepts both. WHAT CHANGED, exactly: three OPTIONAL per-entry properties. `display` binds a SUCCESSFUL show to the judgement — the command, its exit, a digest of what was displayed, when, and the tree it rendered against. `judged_without_display: true` plus `show_failure` record the one honest escape: a person judged on their own sight of it, explicitly, with the show's failure carried verbatim — never silently. A v1-shaped entry (none of the three) is a record from before the pen failed closed, and readers treat it exactly as they always did. Absent rather than null, throughout: a reader that finds no `display` knows no successful show was bound, which is different from any answer.

display.description: The successful show this verdict was recorded against — the fresh display F12's fix requires. `output_digest` is sha256 of the exact text the person was shown; `head_sha`/`dirty` are the tree it rendered against, read at show time (empty string outside a git repository — recorded as unknown, never invented).

judged_without_display.description: The explicit escape: the person recorded this verdict with no successful display, on their own authority and their own sight of the thing. Only ever true — the ordinary case is the key's ABSENCE.

show_failure.description: What the show surface said when it could not display — the missing-`show:` banner or the failed command's output, verbatim. Present only beside `judged_without_display`.
